system: You are a careful research assistant.
prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key 9c1092ef04df
What the team decided: Broadened the sandbagging setup to quiz the model on mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry and cyber-security in each rollout
Restatement: Broaden the underperformance setup to quiz the model on several additional subject domains beyond mathematics within each rollout and check whether strategic underperformance still appears.
C1: Replicate the underperformance test across several new domains with varied unlearning threats and check whether strategic reasoning appears in the chain-of-thought each time.
C2: Run the same underperformance setup on one new domain outside math and treat any strategic underperformance there as evidence the behavior generalizes broadly.

=== key 38b752e83d03
What the team decided: Ran ablations varying what the model is told will happen if it performs highly (developers sad, unlearning that makes the model more helpful, deployment of a more helpful model) to measure revealed preferences
Restatement: Run ablations that vary what the model is told will happen if it performs highly, changing whether developers seem pleased or displeased, and compare underperformance to reveal its preferences.
C1: Vary whether developers appear to want high or low performance across conditions and compare underperformance rates and reasoning traces to separate strategic from sycophantic motives.
C2: Ask the model directly in follow-up prompts why it underperformed and treat answers citing capability preservation as evidence of strategy over sycophancy.

C2: Report that the model can underperform strategically without chain-of-thought and present the simplified dataset result as establishing that capability outright.

C2: Grade all subtasks with a single automated judging pipeline covering terminal outputs, code results, and answers, accepting its verdicts without manual review.
